name: correlation_breakdown_arb_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Highly correlated NIFTY 50 stocks (rolling 20-day correlation > 0.8) occasionally experience intraday correlation breakdowns where one stock moves sharply while its correlated peer stays flat. These breakdowns are typically caused by single large block trades, mutual fund rebalancing, or news misattribution, and the correlation re-establishes within 30-90 minutes as the market digests that no fundamental divergence has occurred. The strategy monitors rolling 30-min intraday correlation and enters when it drops below 0.3 (from a baseline > 0.7), betting on correlation snap-back. The inefficiency persists because monitoring real-time correlation matrices and executing on breakdowns requires infrastructure most retail traders lack.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.

conditions: spread_z < -1.5 (RELIANCE underperforming, buy RELIANCE sell ONGC)
spread_z > 1.5 (RELIANCE outperforming, sell RELIANCE buy ONGC)

exit.signal_exit: if crude oil moves > 2% while in trade, exit (fundamental divergence confirmed)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; high VIX causes legitimate correlation breakdowns
filters.volume_filter: both legs 1-min volume > 10000 shares at entry

weaknesses: RELIANCE is a diversified conglomerate (oil, retail, telecom) while ONGC is pure-play upstream oil; genuine business divergences are common and the correlation baseline may be overstated
The 30-bar rolling correlation window is noisy with 1-min data; random price fluctuations can trigger false correlation breakdown signals
Low signal frequency (1-2 trades/day at best) means the strategy is capital-inefficient and may need to be combined with other strategies to justify monitoring infrastructure
prior_art: Cont & Bouchaud (2000) correlation dynamics; Lillo & Mantegna (2005) correlation-based trading. Adapted for intraday Indian energy sector pair with crude oil filter.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
